title: Magnetic flux
scope: Independent bounded display-pixel review of N124 only, not NOT10p N124; six existing offline course-display screenshots.
observations: Both whole-page images visibly identify the lesson as Magnetic flux and show Printed page 298. The introductory English text, bold definition, following explanatory paragraphs, and final paragraph render as readable text, not blank blocks or raw math markup.

The English definition names the magnitude of magnetic induction, area S, and cosine of the angle between vector B and vector n. Both whole-page images visibly render Phi = BS cos alpha with number (12-1), and Phi = B_n S with number (12-2); the Phi and alpha glyphs, equality signs, and n subscript are present without visible clipping.

Figure 283 is visible between the first formula and the normal-component explanation. Its centered English caption Figure 283 is readable and separated from the drawing and following paragraph on desktop and mobile.

At the bound desktop figure width of 480, the B letter body has both bowls and its overhead rightward vector-arrow shaft and arrowhead are visible. The n letter body and its separate overhead rightward vector-arrow shaft and arrowhead are also visible. Neither body nor accent is missing, replaced by a fallback box, or clipped at the figure boundary.

At the bound mobile figure width of 358, the smaller B and n letter bodies remain recognizable, and both overhead vector-arrow accents retain visible shafts and rightward tips. The n accent sits above the letter rather than being lost against the nearby diagonal line; both labels stay inside the image with visible surrounding space.

The native KaTeX label requirement was checked visually for both letter bodies and accents, not merely for the presence of diagram arrows. The supplied display report separately records loaded KaTeX_Main and KaTeX_Math faces and actual deterministic font evidence for both views; pixels alone do not establish font-file identity.

The final visible English text defines crossings along the chosen normal as positive and against it as negative, describes flux as a directed count, and explicitly states that reversing the normal reverses the sign. It also distinguishes the direction-ignoring geometrical count as the magnitude, unchanged by reversing the normal. These complete sentences remain readable in both whole-page images.

Desktop text stays in its centered reading column; mobile text wraps within visible side margins. The formulas fit the mobile column, the figure stays within the content width, and neither whole-page image shows unintended horizontal overflow, colliding text, missing rendering, or clipped final lines.

The two filenames containing polarization-viewport show the opening Magnetic flux viewport, not a polarization section. The mobile opening viewport ends through formula (12-1) at the screenshot's bottom edge; the mobile whole-page image shows the complete formula and following content, so this is a viewport boundary rather than evidence of unintended content clipping.

perViewJudgments.judgment: Complete visible lesson sequence is readable: title, opening prose, bold definition, formulas (12-1) and (12-2), Figure 283 and caption, projection explanation, and signed/directed-flux conclusion. No blank section, overlap, unintended clipping, or horizontal overflow is visible.

Opening viewport shows Magnetic flux, Printed page 298, the English definition and complete formula (12-1), Figure 283 with visible B and n vector accents, its caption, and the beginning of the projection explanation. No polarization content is claimed; content below the viewport is assessed in the whole-page image.

Existing figure-only capture shows complete B and n bodies and both overhead vector arrows, readable alpha, and intact visible diagram strokes and arrowheads. Labels and accents do not collide or touch the image boundary; there is no missing glyph or blank render.

English prose wraps cleanly in the narrow column. Both numbered formulas, the Figure 283 caption, and the complete final signed-flux paragraph remain visible and readable. B and n accents remain visible in the figure; no unintended overflow, overlap, or terminal clipping is visible.

Opening title, page identifier, introductory prose, inline vectors, and multi-line bold definition remain readable within the side margins. The screenshot boundary cuts through formula (12-1) at the bottom, intentionally limiting this view; the already-reviewed whole-page capture shows the formula intact. This is not a polarization view.

At the actual mobile width, B and n letter bodies and their overhead rightward vector-arrow shafts and tips are visible and unclipped. Alpha and the diagram arrowheads remain distinguishable; the figure is nonblank with no observed label overlap or boundary truncation.
